extracted.intended_audience: authors and researchers submitting to Nature and Nature Portfolio journals; institutional press officers; journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Journal editorial guidelines governing communication with the media, press-release handling, embargo rules, and acceptable scientist-to-scientist communications (including preprints and conference presentations) for Nature and Nature Portfolio journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discouragement of direct media solicitation during submission
rubrics_metrics.description: We strongly discourage authors and potential authors from direct solicitation of media coverage of material they have submitted to Nature and the Nature Portfolio journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions. Refer to 'Communications between scientists' for embargo implications regarding conference presentations and preprints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for discussing accepted contributions with media
rubrics_metrics.description: Accepted contributions can be discussed with the media only once the publication date has been confirmed and no more than a week before the publication date under our embargo conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should not engage media about accepted papers earlier than this window; see communications-between-scientists guidance for preprints/conference exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press-release production and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: We produce and distribute press releases summarizing upcoming content to a list of registered journalists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists are encouraged to read the full version of any papers they wish to cover, and are given the names and contact details of corresponding authors. They receive access to the full text about a week before publication on a password-protected website, together with other relevant material (for example, an accompanying News and Views article, and any extra images).

rubrics_metrics.name: Embargo specificity and enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The content of the press release and papers is embargoed until the time and date clearly stated on the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embargoed material must not be publicly disclosed before the stated embargo time and date; journalists who break embargoes may be removed from press-release circulation lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highlighting especially newsworthy papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers that are deemed especially newsworthy are highlighted by a brief summary on the press release for that journal, written by the editors and the press office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such highlighting may prompt calls or emails to authors; authors are encouraged to cooperate so media coverage is accurate and balanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authors arranging their own publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors whose papers are scheduled for publication may also arrange their own publicity (for instance through their institutional press offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They must strictly adhere to our media embargo and are advised to coordinate their own publicity with our press office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale for embargo policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our policy is to release information about our content in a way that provides fair and equal access to the media, allowing it to provide informed comment based on the complete and final version of the paper that is to be published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach helps authors and institutional press offices interact with the media ahead of publication and benefits from subsequent coverage; it also preserves journalists' ability to obtain independent reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harm from premature release
rubrics_metrics.description: Premature release to the media denies journalists that confidence. It also removes journalists' ability to obtain informed reactions about the work from independent researchers in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This explains why embargoes exist and why adherence is expected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions for embargo breaches by journalists
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists who break our embargoes have been removed from the press-release circulation list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nature Portfolio will continue to use this sanction when appropriate to enforce embargo compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for open communication between researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature Portfolio journals do not wish to hinder communication among researchers. We support open communications between researchers whether on a recognised community preprint server or preprint commenting platforms, through discussions at research meetings or online collaborative sites such as wikis or the author's blog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neither conference presentations nor posting on recognized preprint servers constitute prior publication; see linked preprint policy pages for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media responses to preprints and conference presentations
rubrics_metrics.description: Researchers may respond to requests from the media in response to a preprint or conference presentation, by providing explanation or clarification of the work, or information about its context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such media coverage will not hinder editorial handling of the submission, but may reduce or pre-empt coverage at time of publication. Researchers approached by reporters should make clear the work has not yet undergone peer review, that findings are provisional and conclusions may change. Authors are expected to keep peer review and editorial process details confidential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint posting does not preempt submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientists may display drafts of their research papers on an established preprint server before or during submission to Nature or any Nature journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposure of preprints on servers does not preempt their submission; Nature respects preprint servers and provides further linked guidance on preprint policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to reporters covering preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: We also recommend that reporters who cover preprints clearly indicate that the study has not been peer reviewed and that the claims may change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is to ensure accurate public understanding when provisional results are discussed prior to peer review.
